rubrics.criterion: After the patch, reading workflow inputs is confined to the single input-handling module: every pipeline subsystem that previously read a workflow input at its point of use (orchestration, credential setup, repository preparation, commit, branch push, tag) now obtains its input-derived values from the typed inputs contract (the typed inputs object or parameters derived from it), and no production module outside the input-handling layer performs its own workflow-input reads.
rubrics.rationale: The defining outcome of this case: the deployment-configuration reading responsibility, scattered by the bypass fragments, returns to one owner so that a semantic change to one input is made in exactly one place.

rubrics.criterion: The repository-preparation subsystem (the function performing the clone/orphan preparation and asset copy, such as setRepo) resolves the publish directory, destination subdirectory, publish branch, keep-files, force-orphan, and exclude-assets values from the inputs data it receives (its Inputs parameter), with no direct workflow-input reads left in it.
rubrics.rationale: Repository preparation is the largest bypass cluster in this instance (six preparation options re-read locally); leaving any of them re-read keeps the preparation phase a second definition of those inputs' behavior.

rubrics.criterion: The commit, branch-push, and tag phases (the commit, push, and pushTag functions of the git utilities module) consume their operating decisions from their parameters or typed inputs with no direct workflow-input reads: the empty-commit allowance comes from the accepted argument, the push target and force selection from the accepted arguments, and the tag name and tag message from the accepted arguments with the 'Deployment <tag>' default still applied when no message is provided.
rubrics.rationale: The versioning trio (commit, push, pushTag) is where the bypass left accepted-but-ignored parameters; each phase is an independent fragment site and each must be re-wired to its own declaration, not just the first one found.

rubrics.criterion: The credential-setup subsystem (the auth dispatch function and the SSH key write function, such as setTokens and setSSHKey in the credential-setup module) selects the auth method from the typed Inputs object it receives (deploy key first, then generated GitHub token, then personal token) and writes the SSH key material from that object's deploy key field, with no direct workflow-input reads in the dispatch or the SSH key path.
rubrics.rationale: The auth dispatch and the SSH key write were credential fragments bypassing the typed contract; values sourced elsewhere here silently change the transport and the material used for the push.

rubrics.criterion: The top-level orchestration (the run function of the main module) uses the typed inputs object for both decisions it previously re-derived: it forwards the object's credential fields to the fork-skip guard (the fork helper such as skipOnFork), and drives the nojekyll marker decision from the object's Jekyll decision (passed to the marker helper such as addNoJekyll), without re-deriving either decision from raw workflow-input reads.
rubrics.rationale: The orchestration fragments re-checked credentials and re-implemented the Jekyll toggles inline; a complete repair threads the typed values through the call flow instead of only moving or renaming the reads.

rubrics.criterion: Every orchestration call site is consistent with the repaired implementations: the fork guard, credential setup, repository preparation, commit, push, and tag calls receive their values from the typed inputs object the orchestration holds, with no leftover locally re-read values being forwarded and no dangling read locals left behind.
rubrics.rationale: A frequent partial repair fixes the callees but leaves call sites still feeding re-read locals; the typed contract only holds when the data flowing into every phase of one deployment comes from the single parsed snapshot.

rubrics.criterion: Repaired production functions keep accepting and honoring every parameter declaration that callers and the imported unit tests pass today: a function taking a branch, flag, tag name, tag message, option string, or Inputs object uses those arguments in its behavior (or is restructured in a way that stays argument-compatible with the existing tests and callers).
rubrics.rationale: The pipeline functions' arguments are the typed contract's delivery mechanism and are asserted directly by tests with explicit values; silently ignoring or dropping them is both a behavioral break and an incomplete association.

rubrics.criterion: Duplicated input-parsing policy artifacts remain in the pipeline modules after the repair, such as the module-local boolean-coercion helper that the git utilities module gained, or inline copies of the boolean parsing expression left in the orchestration or preparation code.
rubrics.rationale: The bypass introduced local re-implementations of the input parsing convention; leaving any copy behind keeps the convention defined in several places even after the direct reads are gone.

rubrics.criterion: Bypass bookkeeping artifacts survive the repair: the targeted unused-parameter suppression comments introduced where the branch-push and tag functions stopped honoring their arguments, or equivalent accepted-but-ignored parameters, are still present after the patch.
rubrics.rationale: Suppression comments and ignored-argument declarations are direct fingerprints of the scattered reads; a complete cleanup removes them together with the reads that motivated them.

rubrics.criterion: The Jekyll publishing behavior or its mutual-exclusion guard regressed: for example, the nojekyll marker is now written when a Jekyll toggle is enabled (or not written when it is disabled), or a workflow enabling both Jekyll options no longer fails with the documented mutual-exclusion error.
rubrics.rationale: The Jekyll fragment in the orchestration is the trickiest re-derivation in this instance; a careless consolidation can invert the boolean logic or drop the mutual-exclusion failure the input layer must still raise first.

rubrics.criterion: The credential dispatch regressed: the repaired auth selection picks a different transport or fails differently for some credential combination (deploy key must take precedence over the generated GitHub token, which must take precedence over the personal token, and no credential at all must still fail with the not-found error), or the same-branch and external-repository protections of the token path were weakened.
rubrics.rationale: The auth fragment bypassed the typed credential fields; an inconsistent repair can reorder the dispatch chain or drop the guard semantics, producing a different remote URL for an unchanged workflow.

rubrics.criterion: Commit, tag, or push semantics drifted in the repair: an empty tag name no longer results in a no-op, the 'Deployment <tag>' default message is no longer used for an unconfigured tag message, force-push happens without the force-orphan option, or an orphan branch is created when force-orphan is unset.
rubrics.rationale: The versioning phases carried operational values from raw reads; the repair must restore parameter-driven behavior without flipping these explicitly documented default and flag behaviors.

rubrics.criterion: The repair weakened the compatibility boundary instead of refactorings within it: the action manifest's declared input surface changed (names, defaults, or documented semantics), the input-handling layer stopped parsing some declared input into the typed object, or existing test files were modified or removed to make the suite pass.
rubrics.rationale: This Action's verified behavior is defined by the manifest inputs, the single input layer's parsing, and the untouched test suite; trading any of those away is an out-of-boundary shortcut rather than the requested consolidation.
